name: Gorilla Row — Alternating Kettlebell
description: The gorilla row is performed with two kettlebells on the floor in a hip-hinge position, alternating rows with each arm while the other holds the kettlebell stationary on the floor. The alternating action requires significant anti-rotation core stability, as the shifting load constantly challenges the obliques. The ground-based starting position adds a natural dead-stop at each repetition, eliminating momentum between reps.

execution.starting_position: Place two matching kettlebells on the floor, positioned shoulder-width apart. Stand between them and hinge at the hips to approximately parallel. Grip both kettlebells while maintaining a neutral spine.
execution.setup_instructions: Use matching kettlebells. The hip hinge position must be maintained throughout the entire set.
steps: Step 1: Hinge to roughly parallel, gripping both kettlebells on the floor.
Step 2: Brace the core hard against the anti-rotation demand.
Step 3: Row one kettlebell to the hip while the other stays on the floor.
Step 4: Return the rowed kettlebell to the floor under control.
Step 5: Immediately row the other side. Continue alternating.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on each row, maintain bracing between alternating reps.
common_mistakes: Rotating the hips when switching arms — maintain square hips
Letting the stationary kettlebell move on the floor
Rising out of the hip hinge during the set
safety_considerations: The hip hinge must be maintained for the duration — fatigue causing the torso to rise places greater lumbar load
Ensure kettlebells will not tip — use flat-bottomed kettlebells on a flat surface
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Kettlebell returns to floor between each rep, pulled to hip level at the top.
coaching_cues: Dead stop each rep on the floor
Brace your core like you're taking a punch
